html:
The Malla dynasty ruled the Kathmandu valley in Nepal from about 1201 to 1769. In the 15th century the kingdom split into three rival city kingdoms: Kathmandu, Patan and Bhaktapur.

The Malla age was the golden age of Newar culture. Each city built a royal Durbar Square crowded with tiered temples, palaces and water spouts, in brick and carved wood. Jayasthiti Malla, in the late 14th century, is remembered for ordering society into castes. Newar artists such as Araniko carried their skills to Tibet and China.

The rivalry of the three cities left them weak. Prithvi Narayan Shah of Gorkha took them one by one between 1768 and 1769 and made Kathmandu the capital of a unified Nepal. Their squares are now World Heritage Sites, badly hit by the earthquake of 2015.
